department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

deadline.value: General Fall priority admission and merit-based funding deadline is January 15 (applied automatically with the admission application); general international Fall deadline is May 15.
deadline.quote: Priority Admission Application Deadline / Priority Funding Deadline (applies only to Fall semester admissions): January 15 | International Student Admission Application Deadline: May 15

gre_general.value: GRE scores are listed as an admission requirement for the Electrical Engineering Ph.D. program.
gre_general.quote: Ph.D. Program Additional Admission Requirements: ... GRE scores

gre_subject.value: ETS does not offer a GRE Subject Test in Electrical and Computer Engineering.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Neither the Electrical Engineering Ph.D. page nor the Graduate Catalog states whether a pre-admission supervisor commitment is required.

funding.value: Engineering Ph.D. students compete for College of Engineering GRAs/GTAs and Graduate College Doctoral GTAs ($20,000 minimum 9-month stipend plus tuition and health insurance).
funding.quote: Graduate Research Assistantships (GRAs) are available to M.S. and Ph.D. students. ... Availability of GRAs is dependent on faculty research areas and funding/grant status. | Academic background and familiarity with course content will play a role in selection for GTA positions.

also.quote: However, currently only a portion of qualified students will be supported as GTAs.

entry_route.value: Open directly to applicants with a B.S. in electrical/computer engineering (3.5+ GPA over the last 60 credit hours) as well as M.S. holders in ECE or a related field.
entry_route.quote: Bachelor’s degree in electrical/computer engineering from an ABET accredited university or from an acceptable institution of higher learning with an earned GPA of 3.5 or higher over the last 60 course credit hours of undergraduate degree or Master of Science in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related discipline from an acceptable institution of higher learning, and prior research experience.

notes: Tracks: Computer Engineering, Communications and Signal Processing, Electronic and Optical Materials and Devices, and Power Systems and Control.
